rationale: Start with a broad gradient to locate the elution window and critical pairs while minimizing the risk of missing strongly retained compounds. A moderate temperature leaves room to tune selectivity in either direction.

Increase temperature while keeping the gradient fixed to test selectivity of the sole unresolved pair. The current last peak is comfortably below 10 minutes, so prioritize improving resolution without slowing the gradient.

Test a lower temperature to shift selectivity in the opposite direction; the similar critical-pair resolutions at 40 and 50 °C may conceal an elution-order reversal. Keep the gradient unchanged to isolate temperature effects while retaining time headroom.

Test higher-temperature selectivity with a shallower gradient to spread the central peak cluster and protect neighboring separations. The earlier final elution at higher temperature provides room to extend the gradient while targeting a last peak below 10 minutes.

Injection 4 reached the maximum CRF; shorten the gradient by one grid step to seek a faster fully resolved method. Keep temperature and endpoints fixed to measure whether the critical pair retains R ≥ 1.5.

Shorten the gradient another step to find the fastest fully resolved method at 55 °C. Monitor both central critical pairs, particularly the pair whose resolution decreased from 2.23 to 1.77 in the previous step.

Return to the fully resolved 14-minute gradient and raise the starting organic fraction one step to accelerate elution. Test whether this narrower gradient window preserves both critical separations while improving on the 8.18-minute last peak.

Use a narrower organic window to obtain a slope between the resolved 14-minute and under-resolved 12-minute methods. This should recover the critical separation while eluting the last peak slightly earlier than injection 5.

Increase the slope slightly from 0.0625 to 0.065 organic fraction per minute, targeting faster elution while retaining full resolution. The critical separations are expected to remain just above 1.5, and injection 8 indicates the final peak should elute before this gradient ends.

Lower the starting organic fraction to improve the separation that limited gradient shortening, while using a steeper slope to accelerate the final peak. This tests a potentially faster fully resolved method; injection 9 remains the fastest confirmed maximum-score option.

Reduce the slope from injection 10 to recover the unresolved central pair while retaining the low starting organic fraction. This targets full resolution with a last peak earlier than the 7.76-minute benchmark, though the other critical pair may be close to its limit.

Test a substantially faster, hotter gradient for an alternative selectivity window where the limiting central pair may reverse order and separate again. Injection 11 preserves the maximum-score benchmark if this exploratory method sacrifices resolution.

Explore the fast, high-temperature selectivity window with a higher starting organic fraction and a gentler slope. These changes may redistribute the two crowded central separations while keeping final elution well below the fastest fully resolved benchmark.

Raise the starting organic fraction one step to test whether the remaining central pair separates further in this fast selectivity window. Monitor the first pair and the neighboring central pair for loss of resolution as retention decreases.

Test whether lower-temperature selectivity supports a fast gradient without the central crowding seen at 60 °C. Restore the lower starting organic fraction to protect early-peak resolution; injection 11 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved method.

Test an intermediate low-temperature selectivity window with a low starting organic fraction to spread the central cluster. This explores an alternative to the narrowly resolved 55 °C optimum while using a strong endpoint to avoid truncation.

Raise temperature one step from the fastest confirmed fully resolved method to test whether it can be accelerated without losing full credit. Keeping the gradient fixed isolates temperature selectivity in this promising low-starting-organic region.

Return to 55 °C and test the next steeper endpoint above injection 11 to bracket the fastest fully resolved slope on the instrument grid. The central pair at R 1.59 is the likely limit; retain injection 11 if it falls below 1.5.

Test whether the higher starting organic fraction shifts the 40 °C central cluster into full resolution with a moderately shallow gradient. This explores an alternative maximum-score region while retaining injection 11 as the fastest confirmed fully resolved method.

Raise the starting organic fraction one step to test whether the 40 °C critical pair reaches full resolution while shortening final retention. Injection 19 leaves substantial resolution headroom in the other pairs, including the early peaks.

Refine around the maximum-score region by slowing injection 7’s gradient one step to recover its limiting separation. The higher starting organic fraction may provide more balanced critical-pair margins than injection 11 while keeping the last peak below 10 minutes.

Lower the endpoint one step to make injection 21’s gradient slightly shallower and lift its sole unresolved pair above 1.5. This targets a maximum-score method with better critical-pair margins while keeping final elution below 10 minutes.

Test a slope of 0.0667, just above the fully resolved 0.065 slope of injection 9, to locate the faster-resolution boundary at phi0 0.10. The limiting pair is expected to be close to R = 1.5; injection 11 remains the fastest confirmed maximum-score method.

Shorten injection 11’s programmed gradient while preserving its successful slope and starting composition. The gradient ends at the outlet at 8.65 minutes, after the observed 7.60-minute final peak, so this should retain maximum CRF with a shorter gradient program.

Use the final injection to test a slightly shallower version of injection 22, targeting larger critical-pair margins while keeping the last peak below 10 minutes. Injections 11 and 24 remain the fastest confirmed maximum-score methods if this added resolution costs too much time.
